summary: Implemented Issue #2 per-session FIFO serialization: RlmRuntimeImpl queues same-session evals in submission order (no busy), freezes one total deadline at eval() submission (queue wait consumes it), self-settles queued abort/timeout without touching the running kernel, captures the kernel only at dequeue (fatal eviction => fresh kernel observable), makes dispose terminal by rejecting queued entries and awaiting kernel+drain barriers, and keeps cross-session parallelism. Strict TDD: RED on base e55418b (6 FAIL / 2 PASS focused) then GREEN; full gate PASS (focused 8/8, rlm-loop 94/94, pnpm test 103 pass + 2 live-skipped, typecheck, build, py_compile, check:memory, git diff --check).

GREEN: implemented minimal per-session FIFO in RlmRuntimeImpl (QueuedEval + enqueue/ensureDrain/drainLoop/runEntry/settleEntry/cancelQueued/expireQueued/removeQueued); kept Kernel untouched, kept busy as internal defense, no new public fields, no new source files, no Python kernel change.

Coordinator isolated two follow-ups: (a) lost wakeup when an eval enqueues after the old drain saw an empty queue but before its finally deleted the drains entry - fixed by identity-checked delete then re-ensureDrain if unsettled work remains and runtime not disposed; (b) dispose test hang because onQuery returned a never-settling latch that blocks the Issue #4 child cleanup barrier - fixed in the test to reject on the cell controller abort (deterministic cleanup, contract unchanged). findings: No actionable correctness/contract/test/memory defect; all 10 falsification targets resolved as non-actionable.
Lost-wakeup (src/runtime.ts ensureDrain finally identity-check + re-ensureDrain): sound under single-threaded JS; no uncovered window, at most one drain per session.
Double-settlement/leak: settled flag + once listeners + timer clear on all paths; all settleEntry call sites provide err|out; no unhandled rejection observed.

Abort handoff: enqueue re-check closes precheck/registration; removal->waitReady/evalCell attach is single microtask chain; foreign abort yields queued-cancel (kernel untouched) or active-cancel (Issue #1 semantics). Non-actionable nuance: sub-ms foreign-microtask dispose between waitReady and evalCell settles that entry kind='closed' instead of 'cancel' via runEntry catch - prompt, single settlement, no test/doc contract contradicted.

Dispose race coverage: non-active queued entries rejected synchronously with cancel; active via kernel.dispose barrier or runEntry catch; barrier covers kernels + all live drain workers; no drain created post-dispose.

Fatal eviction: finishCell evict runs synchronously before runEntry resumes, so successor dequeues after eviction; identity-checked onExit prevents stale delete; fresh PID + namespace loss observed in crash test.

Deadline: frozen at eval() submission, queue wait charged; remaining<=0 settles at enqueue with no queue/kernel; near-zero budgets reuse pre-existing Issue #1 startup-deadline semantics (not a new defect).
FIFO/cross-session: per-session queue+drain only, submission order total-ordered, different sessions parallel/isolated.
No new public surface: all queue state private; busy remains unreachable Kernel-internal defense; no Jobs/Workflow/global scheduler.
Docs EN/ZH consistent with implementation; Issue #4 settlement bullets correctly rewritten to queue semantics.
